Lebesgue spatial measure and its coordinate product convention, restricted on boxes, and Euclidean dot products/norms specify the intended normalization. This fixes notation for the standard measure, not an assumption of integrability or a Fubini conclusion. H001 supplies finite dimensions.
Real density is exactly |u_t|² plus the finite sum of spatial derivative squares; D001/D003 and H001/H002 supply all components. No finiteness of its spatial integral is granted.

e_t means the time derivative of D006. H001/H002 make the density differentiable by the ordinary rules for derivatives of finite sums of smooth component products. The definition asserts neither a differentiation-under-integral formula nor its use.
